title: Drinking water maximum contaminant levels study guide
description: Federal MCLs and MRDLs in 40 CFR 141 Subpart G: who they cover, units, compliance basis, dates and best available technologies, with exact quotes.
intro: Subpart G of 40 CFR Part 141 sets the federal maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for organic, inorganic, microbiological, disinfection byproduct and radionuclide contaminants, and the maximum residual disinfectant levels (MRDLs) for chlorine, chloramines and chlorine dioxide. This guide sets out what the rule text states on which systems each limit covers, the units and the compliance basis, the effective and compliance dates, and the best available technologies (BAT) EPA lists. The PFAS entries in 141.61(c)(2) have an effective date of April 26, 2029. Monitoring and analytical methods sit in other subparts and are not covered. States with primacy may adopt stricter limits, so check your State's rules too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: The volatile organic contaminant MCLs in 141.61(a) apply to community and non-transient, non-community water systems.
points.quote: The following maximum contaminant levels for volatile organic contaminants apply to community and non-transient, non-community water systems.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The synthetic organic contaminant MCLs in 141.61(c)(1) and (2), including the PFAS MCLs, apply to community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems.
points.quote: The following maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section for synthetic organic contaminants apply to community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Most inorganic MCLs in 141.62(b) apply to community and non-transient, non-community water systems, but the fluoride MCL in 141.62(b)(1) applies only to community water systems.
points.quote: The maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants specified in paragraphs (b) (2)-(6), (b)(10), and (b) (11)-(16) of this section apply to community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems. The maximum contaminant level specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section only applies to community water systems.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The nitrate, nitrite and total nitrate and nitrite MCLs in 141.62(b)(7) through (9) also apply to transient non-community water systems.
points.quote: The maximum contaminant levels specified in (b)(7), (b)(8), and (b)(9) of this section apply to community water systems; non-transient, non-community water systems; and transient non-community water systems.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Maximum contaminant level goals (MCLGs) and MRDLGs are set in Subpart F, not Subpart G, and are not covered here. Monitoring frequencies, sampling locations and analytical methods are in other subparts of Part 141 and are not covered here.

topics.name: Microbiological contaminants

points.text: Until March 31, 2016, the total coliform MCL was based on presence or absence of total coliforms in a sample, not coliform density.
points.quote: Until March 31, 2016, the total coliform MCL is based on the presence or absence of total coliforms in a sample, rather than coliform density.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Under that pre-2016 rule, a system collecting at least 40 samples a month complied if no more than 5.0 percent of the month's samples were total coliform-positive.
points.quote: For a system that collects at least 40 samples per month, if no more than 5.0 percent of the samples collected during a month are total coliform-positive, the system is in compliance with the MCL for total coliforms.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Beginning April 1, 2016, a system complies with the E. coli MCL for samples taken under subpart Y unless one of the conditions in 141.63(c)(1) through (4) occurs.
points.quote: Beginning April 1, 2016, a system is in compliance with the MCL for E. coli for samples taken under the provisions of subpart Y of this part unless any of the conditions identified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(4) of this section occur.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Two of the conditions are an E. coli-positive repeat sample following a total coliform-positive routine sample, and a total coliform-positive repeat sample following an E. coli-positive routine sample.
points.quote: (1) The system has an E. coli-positive repeat sample following a total coliform-positive routine sample. (2) The system has a total coliform-positive repeat sample following an E. coli-positive routine sample.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The other two conditions are failing to take all required repeat samples after an E. coli-positive routine sample, and failing to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for total coliform.
points.quote: (3) The system fails to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample. (4) The system fails to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for total coliform.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: For public notification under subpart Q, a violation of the E. coli MCL may pose an acute risk to health.
points.quote: For purposes of the public notification requirements in subpart Q of this part, violation of the MCL may pose an acute risk to health.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Beginning April 1, 2016, a public water system determines E. coli MCL compliance for each month in which it is required to monitor for total coliforms.
points.quote: Beginning April 1, 2016, a public water system must determine compliance with the MCL for E. coli in paragraph (c) of this section for each month in which it is required to monitor for total coliforms.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Among the best technology, treatment techniques or other means 141.63(e) lists for coliform MCL compliance are keeping a disinfectant residual throughout the distribution system and proper distribution system maintenance, including cross connection control and continual positive water pressure in all parts of the system.
points.quote: (2) Maintenance of a disinfectant residual throughout the distribution system; (3) Proper maintenance of the distribution system including appropriate pipe replacement and repair procedures, main flushing programs, proper operation and maintenance of storage tanks and reservoirs, cross connection control, and continual maintenance of positive water pressure in all parts of the distribution system;

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.quote: Chloramines 4.0 (as Cl2). Chlorine dioxide 0.8 (as ClO2).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.65, Maximum residual disinfectant levels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: For CWSs and NTNCWSs, subpart H systems serving 10,000 or more had to comply beginning January 1, 2002.
points.quote: CWSs and NTNCWSs. Subpart H systems serving 10,000 or more persons must comply with this section beginning January 1, 2002.

points.quote: control of treatment processes to reduce disinfectant demand and control of disinfection treatment processes to reduce disinfectant levels.

points.text: The MCL for combined radium-226 and radium-228 is 5 pCi/L, found by adding the radium-226 and radium-228 results.
points.quote: The maximum contaminant level for combined radium-226 and radium-228 is 5 pCi/L. The combined radium-226 and radium-228 value is determined by the addition of the results of the analysis for radium-226 and the analysis for radium-228.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.quote: The maximum contaminant level for gross alpha particle activity (including radium-226 but excluding radon and uranium) is 15 pCi/L.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Beta particle and photon radioactivity from man-made radionuclides must not produce an annual dose equivalent to the total body or any internal organ greater than 4 mrem/year.
points.quote: The average annual concentration of beta particle and photon radioactivity from man-made radionuclides in drinking water must not produce an annual dose equivalent to the total body or any internal organ greater than 4 millirem/year (mrem/year).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Except for the radionuclides in table A, the concentration of man-made radionuclides causing 4 mrem must be calculated on the basis of 2 liters per day of drinking water intake, using the 168 hour data list in NBS Handbook 69.
points.quote: Except for the radionuclides listed in table A, the concentration of man-made radionuclides causing 4 mrem total body or organ dose equivalents must be calculated on the basis of 2 liter per day drinking water intake using the 168 hour data list

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If two or more radionuclides are present, the sum of their annual dose equivalents must not exceed 4 mrem/year.
points.quote: If two or more radionuclides are present, the sum of their annual dose equivalent to the total body or to any organ shall not exceed 4 mrem/year.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The uranium MCL is 30 µg/L.
points.quote: The maximum contaminant level for uranium is 30 µg/L.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Community water systems must comply with the radium, gross alpha, beta/photon and uranium MCLs beginning December 8, 2003, with compliance determined under 141.25 and 141.26.
points.quote: Community water systems must comply with the MCLs listed in paragraphs (b), (c), (d), and (e) of this section beginning December 8, 2003 and compliance shall be determined in accordance with the requirements of §§ 141.25 and 141.26.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)
